summary: Windows names now display as item-ID-bound Kit buttons. Double-click or F2 opens the focused Input; Escape discards, and ordinary blur and Enter compare the raw spelling to the entry baseline. Changed drafts go through InlineEdit and the existing conditional store transaction. The runner verified both Windows journeys and the inherited Android/window gates.
evidence: cargo test --locked -p boardcraft-desktop --features native-smoke --test windows_smoke -- --test-threads=1: both required cases passed, zero ignored. The driver dispatched events at presented controls; the parent checked their ordered board/item identities and acknowledged each checkpoint only after a fresh rustday_test read of both rows.

display_edit_cancel_blur_and_enter: single click focused the second Review display. Double-click opened its focused Input; Escape discarded Discard me. F2 reopened Review, and unchanged Enter returned focus to the display. Neither exit launched a submission; both ordered Review rows stayed at revision 1. Blurring raw ' Coral ' to the sibling submitted once, left focus there and committed Coral at revision 2. Re-entering ' Coral ' against Coral submitted once but preserved revision 2. Enter with Review artwork committed revision 3 and returned focus to the second display. The sibling stayed Review/1 throughout.

rejected_edit_then_save_close_and_reopen: blank Enter restored a focused Input containing exactly three spaces, with rejection and Retry visible; both stored rows were unchanged. Blurring the corrected draft to the sibling showed Saving… and the accepted Review label while the second row was locked. The parent checked both revision-1 rows before releasing the lock. Saved then showed Review artwork, with focus still on the sibling. After normal close, a second process showed both accepted labels without editors; fresh reads confirmed the same ordered IDs at revisions 1 and 2.

Operator reference comparison: an isolated run of the real source component with two Review rows observed display on single click, focused input on double-click, and zero save callbacks for Escape and unchanged Enter after F2. Blur to the sibling forwarded one raw ' Coral ' for the second ID against baseline revision 1; changed Enter forwarded Review artwork against revision 2. Separately, the source save operation on disposable data rejected whitespace, trimmed Coral, preserved revision 2 for the padded repeat and committed Review artwork at revision 3. These are component and operation comparisons, not an end-to-end browser session.

Recovery differs: the source cell unmounted on blank Enter and delegated the pending value and failure to its parent. Windows shows only the accepted label while pending and reopens the failed draft for correction. The conditional title check, explicit conflict retry/revert and keyboard focus return are native behavior, not evidence of full source concurrency or recovery parity. Drafts across remounts, Windows touch entry and navigation remain open.

cargo test --locked --workspace passed all eight portable integration cases, including desktop_edit commit failure, retained draft, retry and conflict/revert. Workspace and Android formatting checks passed. Workspace Clippy with native-smoke and warnings denied passed.

The Amber draft resumed in Android PID 8617, local activity c38647. Windows displayed the clean buttons Review sketch (ID 42) and Coral (ID 17) on board fb7067ae-2b50-4286-8283-9718b8b0691a. After force-stop, PID 9053 showed those accepted names without an editor; fresh store reads confirmed revisions 1 and 2.

The ordinary runner dispatched a fresh Astra 6.2 High worker and marked 09-windows-name-cell verified. All 12 runner regressions passed. Operator also ran the complete 03 and 08 packet gates separately: workspace binary build and desktop_edit passed; Android draft resume, same-board Windows labels and cold reopen passed again, as did both native Windows tests.
